title.zh: 卷69 志四十四 地理十六 四川
title.raw: 卷69 志四十四 地理十六 四川

translations.literal: Treatise Forty-Four
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 44

translations.literal: Geography Sixteen
translations.idiomatic: Geography 16

translations.literal: Sichuan
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan

translations.literal: Sichuan: the territory of Liang Province in the Yu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan lay within the domain of Liang as described in the Tribute of Yu.

sentences.zh: 明置四川等處承宣布政使司。

translations.literal: In the Ming, the Sichuan and Other Places Provincial Administration Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming established the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission.

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qing, this arrangement was retained.
translations.idiomatic: The early Qing kept the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，置四川省，設巡撫，治成都。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Sichuan Province was established, a provincial governor was appointed, and the seat was at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1645, Sichuan Province was created with a provincial governor seated at Chengdu.

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, a Sichuan governor-general was additionally established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1657, a governor-general of Sichuan was added.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，改烏撒隸貴州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi, Wusa was transferred to be subordinate to Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1665, Wusa was placed under Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，改設川湖總督，駐湖北荊州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Sichuan-Huguang governor-general was established, stationed at Jingzhou in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In 1668, the post was reorganized as governor-general of Sichuan and Huguang, with headquarters at Jingzhou in Hubei.

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the headquarters were moved to Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670, the headquarters moved to Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 十九年，又改為川陝甘總督，駐陝西西安。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, it was again changed to the Sichuan-Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general, stationed at Xi'an in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In 1680, the office became governor-general of Sichuan, Shaanxi, and Gansu, seated at Xi'an in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，改東川、烏蒙、鎮雄隸雲南，遵義隸貴州，省馬湖入敘州，改建寧衛為寧遠府，升錦、茂、達三州及資縣並為直隸州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong were transferred to Yunnan; Zunyi to Guizhou; Mahu was abolished and merged into Xuzhou; Jianning Guard was converted to Ningyuan Prefecture; and the three prefectures of Jin, Mao, and Da, together with Zi County, were all promoted to directly administered departments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728, Dongchuan, Wumeng, and Zhenxiong were assigned to Yunnan and Zunyi to Guizhou; Mahu was abolished and absorbed into Xuzhou; Jianning Guard became Ningyuan Prefecture; and Jinzhou, Maozhou, Dazhou, and Zi County were all elevated to directly administered departments.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Yazhou was promoted to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1729, Yazhou was elevated to prefectural status.

sentences.zh: 十二年，升嘉定、潼川二州為府，升忠州為直隸州，置黔彭直隸廳。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the two departments of Jiading and Tongchuan were promoted to prefectures; Zhongzhou was promoted to a directly administered department; and the Qianpeng Directly Administered Subprefecture was established.
translations.idiomatic: In 1734, Jiading and Tongchuan became prefectures, Zhongzhou became a directly administered department, and the Qianpeng Directly Administered Subprefecture was created.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年裁，改酉陽土司為酉陽直隸州，升敘永廳為直隸廳。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianlong it was abolished; the Youyang native chieftain domain was converted to the Youyang Directly Administered Department; and Xuyong Subprefecture was promoted to a directly administered subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1736, after an abolition, the Youyang native domain became the Youyang Directly Administered Department and Xuyong Subprefecture was elevated to directly administered status.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復專設四川總督，裁巡撫，以總督兼理巡撫事，治成都。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, a Sichuan governor-general was again established exclusively; the provincial governor was abolished; the governor-general concurrently handled provincial governor affairs; and the seat was at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1749, a dedicated governor-general of Sichuan was restored, the provincial governorship was abolished, and the governor-general took over those duties at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，改松潘衛為松潘直隸廳，改雜古腦為理番直隸廳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Songpan Guard was converted to the Songpan Directly Administered Subprefecture, and Zagunao was converted to the Lifan Directly Administered Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1760, Songpan Guard became the Songpan Directly Administered Subprefecture and Zagunao became the Lifan Directly Administered Subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，改石砫土司為石砫直隸廳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the Shizhu native chieftain domain was converted to the Shizhu Directly Administered Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1761, the Shizhu native domain became the Shizhu Directly Administered Subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年，升達州為綏定府。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing, Dazhou was promoted to Suining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1802, Dazhou was elevated to Suining Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十年，升打箭爐廳為直隸廳。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Guangxu, Dajianlu Subprefecture was promoted to a directly administered subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1904, Dajianlu Subprefecture became a directly administered subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，設督辦川滇邊務大臣，駐巴塘。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, a commissioner for Sichuan-Yunnan border affairs was established, stationed at Batang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1906, a commissioner to oversee Sichuan-Yunnan border affairs was appointed at Batang.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，改敘永廳為永寧直隸州，升打箭爐廳為康定府，升巴安縣為巴安府。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, Xuyong Subprefecture was converted to the Yongning Directly Administered Department; Dajianlu Subprefecture was promoted to Kangding Prefecture; and Ba'an County was promoted to Ba'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1908, Xuyong Subprefecture became the Yongning Directly Administered Department, Dajianlu became Kangding Prefecture, and Ba'an County became Ba'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，改德爾格忒土司為登科府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, the Dergete native chieftain domain was converted to Dengke Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 1909, the Dergete native domain became Dengke Prefecture.

translations.literal: To the east, to Badong County in Hubei;
translations.idiomatic: On the east, to Badong County in Hubei;

translations.literal: one thousand seven hundred sixty li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 1,760 li.

translations.literal: To the west, to the Tibetan border of Xining in Gansu;
translations.idiomatic: On the west, to the Tibetan frontier of Xining in Gansu;

translations.literal: one thousand two hundred forty li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 1,240 li.

translations.literal: To the south, to Yuanmou County in Yunnan;
translations.idiomatic: On the south, to Yuanmou County in Yunnan;

translations.literal: two thousand thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 2,030 li.

translations.literal: To the north, to Ningqiang Department in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: On the north, to Ningqiang in Shaanxi.

translations.literal: one thousand one hundred eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: a distance of 1,180 li.

sentences.zh: 廣三千里，袤三千二百里。

translations.literal: It is three thousand li wide and three thousand two hundred li long.
translations.idiomatic: It measures 3,000 li from east to west and 3,200 li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 由康定府至前藏拉薩，駐藏辦事大臣駐。

translations.literal: From Kangding Prefecture to Lhasa in front Tibet, where the Qing resident commissioner in Tibet is stationed.
translations.idiomatic: From Kangding Prefecture to Lhasa in central Tibet, seat of the Qing resident commissioner in Tibet,

translations.literal: four thousand seven hundred ten li.
translations.idiomatic: is a distance of 4,710 li.

sentences.zh: 北極高二十七度五十四分至三十二度二十二分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude from twenty-seven degrees fifty-four minutes to thirty-two degrees twenty-two minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Latitude ranges from 27°54′ N to 32°22′ N.

sentences.zh: 京師偏西六度五十三分至十四度十二分。

translations.literal: West of the capital from six degrees fifty-three minutes to fourteen degrees twelve minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Longitude west of Beijing ranges from 6°53′ to 14°12′.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，編戶五百四萬一千七百八十，口五千二百八十四萬四百四十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, registered households numbered five million forty-one thousand seven hundred eighty, and population five hundred twenty-eight million four hundred four thousand four hundred forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In 1911, registered households totaled 5,041,780 and population 52,840,446.

sentences.zh: 都領府十五，直隸州九，直隸廳三，州十一，廳十一，縣百十八，土司二十九。

translations.literal: In all it administered fifteen prefectures, nine directly administered departments, three directly administered subprefectures, eleven departments, eleven subprefectures, one hundred eighteen counties, and twenty-nine native chieftain domains.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised fifteen prefectures, nine directly administered departments, three directly administered subprefectures, eleven departments, eleven subprefectures, 118 counties, and 29 native chieftain domains.

translations.literal: Its famous mountains: in the northeast is Boshong.
translations.idiomatic: Notable mountains include Boshong in the northeast.

translations.literal: Winding along the Sichuan-Shaanxi border is Ba Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Ba Mountain winds along the Sichuan-Shaanxi border.

sentences.zh: 西北自岷分二支：南迤於大金川東西者，青城、蒙、瓘眉，在西者，噶察克拉嶺、折多山；

translations.literal: In the northwest, from Min two branches divide: those extending south on both sides of the Great Jin River are Qingcheng, Meng, and Guanmei; those to the west are Gachakala Ridge and Zheduo Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: In the northwest, Min River splits into two ranges: south of the Great Jin River lie Qingcheng, Meng, and Guanmei; to the west lie Gachakala Ridge and Zheduo Mountain;

sentences.zh: 其在岷東南迤者，摩天嶺、劍門山。

translations.literal: those extending southeast of Min are Motian Ridge and Jianmen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: southeast of Min are Motian Ridge and Jianmen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 碩古里，自青海東巴顏喀喇分支。

translations.literal: Shuoguli branches from Bayan Har on the east of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Shuoguli branches east from Bayan Har in Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 其大川：金沙、鴉龍、岷、嘉陵、渠、涪江，大渡河。

translations.literal: Its great rivers: Jinsha, Yalong, Min, Jialing, Qu, Fujiang, and Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: Major rivers include the Jinsha, Yalong, Min, Jialing, Qu, Fujiang, and Dadu.

translations.literal: Shipping routes: along the eastern border from Kui to Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Water routes ran along the eastern border from Kui to Xu.

sentences.zh: 驛路：自成都東北逾劍閣達陝西沔縣，西渡瀘定橋逾大雪山達西藏江卡。

translations.literal: Postal routes: from Chengdu northeast crossing Jian Pass to Mian County in Shaanxi; west crossing Luding Bridge and the Great Snow Mountain to Jiangka in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: Postal roads ran northeast from Chengdu over Jian Pass to Mian County in Shaanxi, and west across Luding Bridge and the Great Snow Mountains to Jiangka in Tibet.

translations.literal: Railway: Sichuan-Hankou, not yet completed.
translations.idiomatic: Railway: the Sichuan-Hankou line, still under construction.

sentences.zh: 電線：自成都東達漢口，西達打箭爐。

translations.literal: Telegraph lines: from Chengdu east to Hankou, west to Dajianlu.
translations.idiomatic: Telegraph lines ran east from Chengdu to Hankou and west to Dajianlu.

translations.literal: Chengdu Prefecture: strategically important, populous, and difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu Prefecture: strategically important, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Ming dynasty, prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A prefecture under the Ming.

translations.literal: Seat of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Seat of the Cheng-Mian-Long-Mao Circuit.

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu the circuit intendant was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1908 the circuit intendant was abolished.

sentences.zh: 布政使、提學使、提法使、鹽運使，巡警道、勸業道，將軍、副都統、提督駐。

translations.literal: The provincial treasurer, education commissioner, judicial commissioner, salt controller, constabulary circuit intendant, and industry promotion circuit intendant, together with the general, deputy lieutenant-general, and provincial military commander, were stationed here.
translations.idiomatic: It housed the provincial treasurer, education commissioner, judicial commissioner, salt controller, constabulary and industry promotion circuit intendants, and the general, deputy lieutenant-general, and provincial military commander.

translations.literal: Formerly it administered six departments and twenty-five counties.
translations.idiomatic: It formerly governed six departments and twenty-five counties.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，省羅江入德陽，省彰明入綿。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, Luojiang was abolished and merged into Deyang, and Zhangming into Mian.
translations.idiomatic: In 1659, Luojiang was merged into Deyang and Zhangming into Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，省崇寧入郫，省彭入新繁。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, Chongning was abolished and merged into Pi, and Peng into Xinfan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1662, Chongning was merged into Pi County and Peng into Xinfan.

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Huayang was abolished and merged into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670, Huayang was merged into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 雍正六年，復設華陽，升綿、茂二州及資縣並為直隸州，以德陽、綿竹、安隸綿，汶川、保隸茂，資陽、仁壽、井研隸資，又省威入保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng, Huayang was re-established; Mian and Mao departments and Zi County were all promoted to directly administered departments; Deyang, Mianzhu, and An were subordinated to Mian; Wenchuan and Bao to Mao; Ziyang, Renshou, and Jingyan to Zi; and Wei was abolished and merged into Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1728, Huayang was restored; Mianzhou, Maozhou, and Zi County became directly administered departments; Deyang, Mianzhu, and An were placed under Mianzhou; Wenchuan and Bao under Maozhou; Ziyang, Renshou, and Jingyan under Zi; and Wei was merged into Bao.

sentences.zh: 六年，復設崇寧、雙流、彭、彰明四縣屬府。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Chongning, Shuangliu, Peng, and Zhangming four counties were re-established as belonging to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Chongning, Shuangliu, Peng, and Zhangming counties were restored to the prefecture.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Zhangming was transferred to belong to Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: In 1729, Zhangming was transferred to Long'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 東北距京師五千七百十里。

translations.literal: Northeast from the capital, five thousand seven hundred ten li.
translations.idiomatic: It lies 5,710 li northeast of the capital.

sentences.zh: 廣二百四十里，袤二百七十里。

translations.literal: It is two hundred forty li wide and two hundred seventy li long.
translations.idiomatic: It measures 240 li from east to west and 270 li from north to south.

sentences.zh: 北極高三十度四十二分。

translations.literal: North polar altitude thirty degrees forty-two minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Latitude is 30°42′ N.

sentences.zh: 京師偏西十二度十六分。

translations.literal: West of the capital twelve degrees sixteen minutes.
translations.idiomatic: Longitude is 12°16′ west of Beijing.

translations.literal: It administered three departments and thirteen counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governed three departments and thirteen counties.

translations.literal: Chengdu: strategically important, populous, and difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu County: strategically important, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Seat county.

translations.literal: Wudan Mountain is in the northwest corner of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wudan Mountain stands in the northwest corner of the city.

translations.literal: West: Longhua Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the west: Longhua Mountain.

translations.literal: North: Tianhui Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north: Tianhui Mountain.

sentences.zh: 郫江自郫縣入，繞城東而南，入華陽，與錦江合，名二江，亦曰都江。

translations.literal: Pi River enters from Pi County, circles the east of the city and turns south, enters Huayang, joins Jin River, and is called the Two Rivers, also called Du River.
translations.idiomatic: The Pi River enters from Pi County, loops east and south around the city into Huayang, joins the Jin River, and is known as the Two Rivers or the Du River.

sentences.zh: 沱江自新繁入，逕縣北，又東流入新都。

translations.literal: Tuo River enters from Xinfan, passes north of the county, then flows east into Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuo River enters from Xinfan, runs north of the county seat, and flows east into Xindu.

sentences.zh: 金水河自城西穿城東出入江。

translations.literal: Jinshui River enters from the west of the city, passes through the east of the city, and exits into the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinshui River enters west of the city, passes through it eastward, and empties into the main stream.

translations.literal: Moke Pool is within the city.
translations.idiomatic: Moke Pool lies within the city walls.

translations.literal: There are Tianhui and Tuojiang two market towns.
translations.idiomatic: Market towns include Tianhui and Tuojiang.

translations.literal: One postal station: Jinguan.
translations.idiomatic: One postal station: Jinguan.

translations.literal: Huayang: strategically important, populous, and difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Huayang County: strategically important, populous, and difficult to govern.

translations.literal: Attached.
translations.idiomatic: Seat county.

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kangxi it was merged into Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In 1670 it was merged into Chengdu.

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng it was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in 1727.

translations.literal: East: Damian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the east: Damian Mountain.

translations.literal: West: West Mountain, also called Snow Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: To the west: West Mountain, also known as Snow Ridge.

translations.literal: South: Liudui and Tielu.
translations.idiomatic: To the south: Liudui and Tielu.

sentences.zh: 錦江一名汶江，自郫縣入，逕城南，折而東，會成都之郫江。

translations.literal: Jin River, also called Wen River, enters from Pi County, passes south of the city, turns east, and joins Chengdu's Pi River.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin River, also called the Wen River, enters from Pi County, runs south of the city, turns east, and joins Chengdu's Pi River.

sentences.zh: 又折而西，新開河自雙流來會，下流入彭山。

translations.literal: It turns west again; Xinkai River comes from Shuangliu to join it, and downstream flows into Pengshan.
translations.idiomatic: It then turns west; the Xinkai River joins it from Shuangliu, and the combined stream flows down into Pengshan.

sentences.zh: 浣花溪在城東南，一名百花潭。

translations.literal: Huanhua Stream is southeast of the city, also called Baihua Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Huanhua Stream lies southeast of the city, also known as Baihua Pool.

translations.literal: Postal stations are the same as Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: It shares postal stations with Chengdu.

translations.literal: Shuangliu: strategically important.
translations.idiomatic: Shuangliu: strategically important.

translations.literal: Forty li southwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Forty li southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi it was merged into Xinjin.
translations.idiomatic: In 1662 it was merged into Xinjin.

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongzheng it was re-established.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in 1728.

translations.literal: South: Yingtian and Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: To the south: Yingtian and Yicheng.

translations.literal: Southeast: Puxian Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast: Puxian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 新開河自溫江入，逕城南，東流入華陽。

translations.literal: Xinkai River enters from Wenjiang, passes south of the city, and flows east into Huayang.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinkai River enters from Wenjiang, runs south of the city, and flows east into Huayang.

sentences.zh: 石魚河、楊柳河亦自溫江入，逕城西南，合流入新津注大江。

translations.literal: Shiyu River and Yangliu River also enter from Wenjiang, pass southwest of the city, join and flow into Xinjin to enter the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu and Yangliu rivers also enter from Wenjiang, pass southwest of the city, unite, and flow through Xinjin into the Yangtze.

translations.literal: Wenjiang: populous.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjiang: populous.

translations.literal: Fifty li slightly south of west from the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty li west-southwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: North: Nülang and Damu two mountains.
translations.idiomatic: To the north: Nülang and Damu mountains.

sentences.zh: 岷江俗名溫江，即金馬河，自灌縣入，西南入新津。

translations.literal: Min River, commonly called Wen River, that is the Jinma River, enters from Guan County and flows southwest into Xinjin.
translations.idiomatic: The Min River, locally called the Wen River or Jinma River, enters from Guan County and flows southwest into Xinjin.

sentences.zh: 石魚河在城西，自金馬河分流，楊柳河自石魚河分流。

translations.literal: Shiyu River is west of the city; it branches from the Jinma River; Yangliu River branches from Shiyu River.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiyu River lies west of the city, branching from the Jinma River; the Yangliu River in turn branches from the Shiyu River.

sentences.zh: 又酸棗河自郫縣入，東流逕城北，俱入雙流。

translations.literal: Also, Suanzao River enters from Pi County, flows east passing north of the city, and both enter Shuangliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Suanzao River also enters from Pi County, flows east past the north side of the city, and both rivers pass into Shuangliu.

translations.literal: Xinfan: populous.
translations.idiomatic: Xinfan: populous.

translations.literal: Fifty-six li northwest of the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-six li northwest of the prefectural seat.

translations.literal: Northwest: Wulong and Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: To the northwest: Wulong and Pingyang.

translations.literal: North: Quchi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the north: Quchi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 沱江即北江，自郫縣入，逕城南，入成都。

translations.literal: Tuo River is the North River; it enters from Pi County, passes south of the city, and enters Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuo River, also called the North River, enters from Pi County, runs south of the city, and flows into Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 北：清白江，即古湔水，自彭縣入，東入新都。

translations.literal: North: Qingbai River, that is the ancient Jianshui, enters from Peng County and flows east into Xindu.

translations.idiomatic: The Jin River enters from Chonghua, runs southeast of the colony, merges with the Lesser Jin River, turns southwest toward Dajianlu, and becomes the Dadu River.

sentences.zh: 崇化屯廳西二百五十里。

translations.literal: Chonghua Garrison Subprefecture, two hundred fifty li west.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghua Garrison Subprefecture lay 250 li to the west.

translations.literal: East: Gu'er Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: To the east: Gu'er Cliff.

translations.literal: Southeast: Danga Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast: Danga Mountain.

translations.literal: Northeast: Muguomu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast: Muguomu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 金川河自綏靖入，逕屯西入章谷。

translations.literal: The Jin River enters from Suijing, passes west of the colony, and enters Zhanggu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin River enters from Suijing, runs west of the colony, and flows on into Zhanggu.

sentences.zh: 小溪河發源空卡山，東流入小金川河。

translations.literal: Xiaoxi River rises on Kongka Mountain and flows east into the Lesser Jin River.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaoxi River rises on Kongka Mountain and flows east into the Lesser Jin River.

sentences.zh: 綏靖屯廳西二百七十里。

translations.literal: Suijing Garrison Subprefecture, two hundred seventy li west.
translations.idiomatic: Suijing Garrison Subprefecture lay 270 li to the west.

translations.literal: East: Suowu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the east: Suowu Mountain.

translations.literal: South: Zugu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the south: Zugu Mountain.

translations.literal: Southeast: Gongga Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the southeast: Gongga Mountain.

sentences.zh: 金川河自綽斯甲布土司入，逕屯西入崇化。

translations.literal: The Jin River enters from the Chosjab native chieftain domain, passes west of the colony, and enters Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin River enters from the Chosjab native domain, runs west of the colony, and flows on into Chonghua.

translations.literal: East of the Gekeshi Pacification Commissioner Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lay east of the Gekeshi Pacification Commissioner Subprefecture.

translations.literal: Established in the fifteenth year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: It was established in 1750.

translations.literal: West of the Chosjab Pacification Commissioner Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: It lay west of the Chosjab Pacification Commissioner Subprefecture.

translations.literal: Established in the forty-first year of Qianlong.
translations.idiomatic: It was established in 1776.

translations.literal: East: Yixi Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: To the east: Yixi Mountain.

sentences.zh: 金川河自司境南流入綏靖。

translations.literal: The Jin River enters Suijing from the south within the commissioner's domain.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin River enters Suijing from the southern part of the commissioner's domain.
